TITLE: Glucavia Core Messaging Guide
CONTENT: Glucavia is a once-weekly GLP-1 receptor agonist for adults with type 2 diabetes. Key messages: (1) Glucavia lowers HbA1c by up to 1.8 percentage points from baseline. (2) Patients lost an average of 6.2 kg at 52 weeks. (3) Glucavia demonstrated a reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with established CVD. Position Glucavia after metformin for patients who need both glycemic control and weight reduction.

TITLE: Objection Handling: Access and Prior Authorization
CONTENT: When an HCP raises prior authorization or formulary barriers: acknowledge the burden, confirm the payer, and offer the Glucavia Access Hub (PA form pre-fill, appeal templates, 48-hour turnaround). For step-therapy requirements, document metformin failure and HbA1c above 7.5% in the PA submission. Escalate payers with denial rates above 30% to Market Access.

TITLE: Objection Handling: GI Tolerability
CONTENT: Nausea and vomiting are the most common adverse reactions and are usually mild to moderate and transient. Recommend starting at 0.25 mg and titrating every 4 weeks. Advise patients to eat smaller meals and stop eating when full. Elderly patients may benefit from a slower titration schedule. Do not make comparative safety claims versus competitors.

TITLE: Objection Handling: Cost and Affordability
CONTENT: For self-pay patients, offer the Glucavia Patient Support Program: first month free and up to 40% off the monthly price for eligible patients. Discuss total cost of care, including the potential to reduce the need for additional agents. Never discuss pricing negotiated with specific payers.

TITLE: Competitive Positioning vs Sematra
CONTENT: Glucavia and Sematra are both once-weekly GLP-1 RAs. Glucavia differentiators: proven cardiovascular outcome benefit and a single-dose pen with a simpler titration. Do not disparage competitor products. Focus on patient support services and the CV outcomes label.

TITLE: Field Engagement Guidelines
CONTENT: Tier A HCPs (deciles 8-10) should be engaged at least monthly, Tier B at least quarterly. Any Tier A HCP without a call in 60 days should be prioritized in the next call plan. Record key discussion points and objections in the call note within 24 hours.

TITLE: Medical Information Referral Policy
CONTENT: Off-label questions, pancreatitis, thyroid C-cell tumor risk and pregnancy questions must be referred to Medical Information. Representatives must not answer these directly. Log the referral in CRM.

TITLE: Formulary Update Bulletin May 2026
CONTENT: Effective 1 May 2026, StarHealth moved Glucavia from preferred to non-preferred tier in the West region, requiring prior authorization and documented failure of metformin plus an SGLT2 inhibitor. Field teams in Pune and Mumbai should proactively offer Access Hub support.
